---
title: "080 — Backcasting validation"
---

Validate the calibrated model against the past: replay the **observed** transition rates of the
**last observed transition** (2009 → 2018) through transition-potential models and allocation
parameters that were estimated *without* that transition, then compare the resulting maps against
the survey we actually observed. Substeps:

(a) **estimate patch / allocation parameters** from the earlier observed transitions;
(b) **run the backcast**: many stochastic allocations of the last period, over a set of parameter
    choices, in parallel;
(c) **validate** them against the observed map, and select the parameter set to promote.

## What this does and does not test

Every member starts from the **observed** 2009 map and allocates one period, so this measures
one-step allocation skill. The models (`060`'s hold-out run) and the allocation parameters (a)
have not seen the 2009 → 2018 change; the predictor *selection* in `050` has, which is the one
remaining leak.

The rates fed to the backcast are the **observed** ones (`get_obs_trans_rates()`), so the
*quantity* of change per transition is prescribed, not predicted. What is on trial is therefore
only the **allocation** — whether the model puts the right changes in the right places — plus the
allocator's ability to deliver the prescribed quantity at all.

Two consequences worth stating before any number is read:

- **Non-viable transitions bound the score from above.** Observed change belonging to a
  transition that `040`/`060` dropped can never be reproduced, because `predict_trans_pot()` only
  predicts for viable transitions and `adjusted_trans_pot_v()` inner-joins potentials to rates.
  The `unmodellable` share below quantifies that ceiling.
- **Persistence is not skill.** The great majority of Swiss hectares keep their class across a
  survey interval, so any whole-map agreement statistic is dominated by cells nobody had to get
  right. Every metric here is therefore computed on **change**, not on the map.

## Parallelism

DuckLake takes concurrent writers, so the members are independent processes: each mirai daemon
opens its own connection, allocates one member run and commits its map. The potentials are the
same for every member — same observed anterior map, same models, same predictors — so they are
predicted **once**, onto the hold-out run, before any member starts; the members find them
through the run lineage and do not predict. That prediction is the only step that uses `future`
workers. The scoring in (c) is parallelised the same way, one daemon per member.

Memory per daemon is roughly one copy of the adjusted potentials plus two maps; size
`n_workers` against that, not against the core count.

## Parameters

```{r}
#| label: backcast-params
library(data.table)
library(evoland)

# relative, as the catalog was created: DuckLake rejects the same data path spelled
# differently, so the daemons open it from the same working directory (see `everywhere()`)
db_path <- "ssp-ch.evolanddb"
helpers <- normalizePath(file.path("2026-05-ssp-ch", "R", "allocation.R"))

n_perturbations <- 3L # perturbed parameter sets *in addition to* the best estimate
perturb_sd <- 0.05 # sd of the frac_expander perturbation
n_replicates <- 5L # stochastic allocations per parameter set
seed <- 42L
fuzzy_window <- 11L # odd; evoland's default, ~1 km at 100 m resolution
select_score <- "classif.auc" # must match 060
select_maximize <- TRUE
n_workers <- 8L # mirai daemons for allocation and scoring
n_predict_workers <- 16L # future workers for the one prediction
repredict <- TRUE # re-predict the shared potentials, e.g. after 060 was re-run

# the calibration hold-out registered by 060; this step hangs its runs below it
id_run_holdout <- 2000L
param_run_id <- function(p) id_run_holdout + 100L * as.integer(p)
member_run_id <- function(p, r) param_run_id(p) + as.integer(r)
backcast_kinds <- c("backcast parameters", "backcast replicate")

source(helpers)
db <- evoland_db$new(path = db_path)
db$id_run <- 0L

obs_periods <- sort(db$periods_t[is_extrapolated == FALSE & id_period > 0, id_period])
id_period_final <- max(obs_periods) # the backcast period
id_period_initial <- id_period_final - 1L # observed anterior state of every member
calibration_periods <- setdiff(obs_periods[obs_periods > min(obs_periods)], id_period_final)

stopifnot(
  "need at least three observed periods" = length(calibration_periods) >= 1L,
  "no viable transitions - run 040 (and 060, which reconciles viability)" =
    nrow(db$trans_meta_t[is_viable == TRUE]) > 0L,
  "no hold-out run - run 060-transition-modelling.qmd first" =
    nrow(db$runs_t[id_run == id_run_holdout & kind == "calibration hold-out"]) == 1L
)

message(
  "Backcasting period ", id_period_final, " from observed period ", id_period_initial,
  "; calibration from transitions ending in ", toString(calibration_periods)
)
```

## Observed rates as the backcast demand

Written to run `0`: they are a property of the observed record, not of a scenario, and every
backcast run inherits them through the run lineage. The scenario rates `070` wrote sit on the SSP
leaf runs at the *extrapolated* periods, so the two never resolve to the same
`(id_period, id_trans)` slice.

The unmodellable cells are from deglaciation and relatively rare transitions, respectively.
Glacier change is imposed deterministically below, as in the extrapolation, so the transitions
into and out of glacier are given a zero rate here: allocating them as well would move the same
area twice.

```{r}
#| label: backcast-obs-rates
id_lulc_glacier <- db$lulc_meta_t[name == "glacier", id_lulc]
glacier_trans <- db$trans_meta_t[
  id_lulc_anterior %in% id_lulc_glacier | id_lulc_posterior %in% id_lulc_glacier,
  id_trans
]
obs_rates <- db$get_obs_trans_rates()[id_period == id_period_final]
db$trans_rates_t <- as_trans_rates_t(
  copy(obs_rates)[id_trans %in% glacier_trans, `:=`(rate = 0, count = 0L)]
)

viable_trans <- db$trans_meta_t[is_viable == TRUE]
lulc_names <- db$lulc_meta_t[, .(id_lulc, name)]
trans_names <- db$trans_meta_t[
  lulc_names, on = c(id_lulc_anterior = "id_lulc"), name_anterior := i.name
][
  lulc_names, on = c(id_lulc_posterior = "id_lulc"), name_posterior := i.name
][, .(id_trans, id_lulc_anterior, id_lulc_posterior, name_anterior, name_posterior, is_viable)]

unmodellable <- as.data.table(obs_rates)[trans_names, on = "id_trans", nomatch = NULL][
  ,
  .(cells = sum(count), cells_viable = sum(count[is_viable])),
  by = .(id_trans, name_anterior, name_posterior, is_viable)
][, unmodellable_pct := round(100 * (1 - cells_viable / cells), 2)][]
unmodellable[is_viable == FALSE & cells > 1000][order(-cells)]
```

## (a) Allocation parameters

`create_alloc_params_t(id_period_post = )` measures, per viable transition and per observed
period pair ending in `calibration_periods`, the mean and variance of new-patch area, patch
elongation, and the split between cells that **expand** an existing patch of the target class and
cells that start a **new** patch; it averages over the pairs and returns that best estimate. The
`n_perturbations` further sets each jitter `frac_expander` by a normal draw with sd `perturb_sd`,
clamped to [0, 1], with `frac_patcher` following as `1 - frac_expander`.

Only `frac_expander` is perturbed, so this sweep explores the expander/patcher split and nothing
else. A poor `mean_patch_size` estimate will not show up as parameter sensitivity here; widening
the sweep is a change to `perturb_alloc_params()` only.

```{r}
#| label: backcast-alloc-params
db$id_run <- id_run_holdout
best_estimate <- db$create_alloc_params_t(id_period_post = calibration_periods)
db$id_run <- 0L

perturb_alloc_params <- function(params, sd) {
  jittered <- pmin(1, pmax(0, params$frac_expander + rnorm(nrow(params), sd = sd)))
  copy(params)[, `:=`(frac_expander = jittered, frac_patcher = 1 - jittered)]
}

# `param_set` 1 is the best estimate
set.seed(seed)
alloc_params <- rbindlist(c(
  list(copy(best_estimate)[, param_set := 1L]),
  lapply(seq_len(n_perturbations), function(i) {
    perturb_alloc_params(best_estimate, perturb_sd)[, param_set := 1L + i]
  })
))
param_sets <- sort(unique(alloc_params$param_set))
alloc_params[, .(
  n_trans = .N,
  mean_patch_size = round(mean(mean_patch_size, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
  frac_expander = round(mean(frac_expander, na.rm = TRUE), 3)
), by = param_set]
```

A transition that never produced a new patch (all conversions expanded existing ones) comes back
with `patch_elongation = NA`; `alloc_clumpy_one_period()` substitutes `0.5`, and
`mean_patch_size = 0` is handled as a mono-pixel draw in the C++ patcher. Both are safe, but a
transition in that state has no estimated patch geometry at all — worth knowing before reading
its similarity.

```{r}
#| label: backcast-alloc-params-gaps
alloc_params[param_set == 1L & (is.na(patch_elongation) | mean_patch_size <= 1)][
  trans_names,
  on = "id_trans",
  nomatch = NULL
][, .(id_trans, name_anterior, name_posterior, mean_patch_size, patch_elongation)]
```

## Run registration

```
0 (observed record, observed rates)
└── 2000  calibration hold-out: models (060), shared potentials, glacier change
    ├── 2100  parameter set 1 (best estimate)
    │   ├── 2101 … replicates: only the simulated map
    ├── 2200  parameter set 2 (perturbed)
    …
```

One run per parameter set holding its `alloc_params_t`, and one child run per stochastic
replicate holding only its simulated `lulc_data_t`. The only thing that differs between replicates
of a set is the RNG state.

```{r}
#| label: backcast-register-runs
param_runs <- data.table(
  id_run = param_run_id(param_sets),
  parent_id_run = id_run_holdout,
  description = paste0(
    "Backcast allocation parameter set ", param_sets,
    fifelse(param_sets == 1L, " (best estimate)", " (perturbed)")
  ),
  kind = "backcast parameters",
  param_set = param_sets
)

member_runs <- CJ(param_set = param_sets, replicate = seq_len(n_replicates))[, .(
  id_run = member_run_id(param_set, replicate),
  parent_id_run = param_run_id(param_set),
  description = paste0("Backcast replicate ", replicate, " of parameter set ", param_set),
  kind = "backcast replicate",
  param_set = param_set,
  replicate = replicate,
  seed = seed + 1000L * param_set + replicate
)]

# Re-running replaces this step's own runs; anything else in the block is a hard error.
existing_runs <- db$runs_t
mine <- existing_runs[kind %in% backcast_kinds, id_run]
clash <- setdiff(
  intersect(c(param_runs$id_run, member_runs$id_run), existing_runs$id_run),
  mine
)
stopifnot("backcast run ids collide with runs registered elsewhere" = length(clash) == 0L)
if (length(mine) > 0L) {
  message("Replacing ", length(mine), " backcast runs from an earlier execution.")
}

db$commit(
  as_runs_t(rbind(
    existing_runs[!id_run %in% mine],
    param_runs,
    member_runs,
    fill = TRUE
  )),
  "runs_t",
  "overwrite" # may add columns
)

db$alloc_params_t <- as_alloc_params_t(
  copy(alloc_params)[, id_run := param_run_id(param_set)][, -"param_set"]
)
```

## (b) Run the backcast

### Deterministic glacier change

Glacier transitions are not modelled (`040` excludes glacier as an anterior class): their extent
follows the climate, not the land use drivers, so they are imposed on each simulated map after it
is allocated. In the backcast the imposed change is the **observed** one: every cell that turned
into or out of glacier between the two surveys takes its observed class. It is written to
`det_change_t` on the hold-out run, so every member inherits it; in the extrapolation the same
table carries GloGEM projections instead (`052-ingest-glacier-projections`).

```{r}
#| label: backcast-glacier
glacier_change <- db$get_query(
  "select post.id_coord, post.id_lulc
  from {lulc_read_expr} ant
  inner join {lulc_read_expr} post
    on post.id_coord = ant.id_coord and post.id_period = ant.id_period + 1
  where post.id_period = {id_period_final}
    and ant.id_lulc != post.id_lulc
    and (ant.id_lulc in ({id_lulc_glacier*}) or post.id_lulc in ({id_lulc_glacier*}))",
  lulc_read_expr = db$get_read_expr("lulc_data_t")
)
if (nrow(glacier_change) > 0L) {
  db$commit(
    as_det_change_t(glacier_change[, .(
      id_run = id_run_holdout, id_period = id_period_final, id_coord, id_lulc
    )]),
    det_change_table,
    method = "upsert"
  )
}
glacier_change[, .N, by = id_lulc][lulc_names, on = "id_lulc", nomatch = NULL]
```

### Shared transition potentials

```{r}
#| label: backcast-predict
#| output: false
options("evoland.use_prefetch_predict" = TRUE)
future::plan(future.mirai::mirai_multisession, workers = n_predict_workers)
db$id_run <- id_run_holdout
db$predict_trans_pot(
  id_period_post = id_period_final,
  select_score = select_score,
  select_maximize = select_maximize,
  force = repredict
)
db$id_run <- 0L
future::plan("sequential")
```

### Allocation

One task per member, dispatched to `n_workers` daemons. `allocate_member()` (in
`R/allocation.R`) opens its own connection under the member run, seeds R's RNG with the member's
registered seed — CLUMPY draws through it, so each member is reproducible and independent of the
others and of the scheduling order — allocates, imposes `det_change_t` and commits.

```{r}
#| label: backcast-allocate
#| output: false
mirai::daemons(n_workers)
mirai::everywhere({
  setwd(wd)
  source(helpers)
}, wd = getwd(), helpers = helpers)
allocation_tasks <- mirai::mirai_map(
  member_runs[, .(id_run, seed)],
  function(id_run, seed, db_path, id_period_final, select_score, select_maximize) {
    allocate_member(
      db_path = db_path,
      id_run = id_run,
      id_periods = id_period_final,
      seed = seed,
      select_score = select_score,
      select_maximize = select_maximize
    )
  },
  .args = list(
    db_path = db_path,
    id_period_final = id_period_final,
    select_score = select_score,
    select_maximize = select_maximize
  )
)
allocation_log <- rbindlist(allocation_tasks[.stop])
```

```{r}
#| label: backcast-allocation-log
allocation_log[, .(members = .N, median_seconds = median(seconds), n_det_change = max(n_det_change))]
```

## Simulated end states

Every member must cover the observed grid.

```{r}
#| label: backcast-maps
db$id_run <- NULL # the lineage-free read expression spans all runs
simulated_cells <- db$get_query(
  "select id_run, count(*)::integer as n_cells from {lulc_read_expr}
  where id_run in ({member_runs$id_run*}) and id_period = {id_period_final}
  group by id_run",
  lulc_read_expr = db$get_read_expr("lulc_data_t")
)
db$id_run <- 0L
n_observed_cells <- db$get_query(
  "select count(*)::integer from {lulc_read_expr} where id_period = {id_period_final}",
  lulc_read_expr = db$get_read_expr("lulc_data_t"),
  as_atomic = TRUE
)

stopifnot(
  "an allocated run is missing cells" =
    nrow(simulated_cells) == nrow(member_runs) &&
      all(simulated_cells$n_cells == n_observed_cells)
)
simulated_cells[, .N, by = n_cells]
```

## Quantity check: did the allocator deliver the prescribed change?

The first thing to establish is that the allocator hit the demand it was given. uPAM draws
patches without replacement from the source pool; when the prescribed rate is large relative to
the pool, or `avoid_aggregation` rejects many candidate patches, the pool empties before the quota
is met and the run silently under-delivers. `070` flags the same failure mode for the scenario
rates, where it is worse because the LP pushes rates above the historic envelope.

The realised counts come from `lulc_crosstab_v()`: the member's simulated map against the observed
anterior map it inherits. Glacier transitions are left out: their quantity is imposed, not allocated.

```{r}
#| label: backcast-quantity
realised_counts <- rbindlist(lapply(member_runs$id_run, function(r) {
  db$lulc_crosstab_v(
    id_period_anterior = id_period_initial,
    id_period_post = id_period_final,
    id_run_anterior = r
  )[, id_run := r]
}))[trans_names, on = c("id_lulc_anterior", "id_lulc_posterior"), id_trans := i.id_trans][
  !is.na(id_trans), .(id_run, id_trans, count_realised = n_cells)
]

quantity <- merge(
  CJ(id_run = member_runs$id_run, id_trans = setdiff(viable_trans$id_trans, glacier_trans))[
    as.data.table(obs_rates)[, .(id_trans, count_prescribed = count)],
    on = "id_trans",
    nomatch = NULL
  ],
  realised_counts,
  by = c("id_run", "id_trans"),
  all.x = TRUE
)
quantity[is.na(count_realised), count_realised := 0L]
quantity[, shortfall_pct := 100 * (count_prescribed - count_realised) / count_prescribed]

quantity[
  ,
  .(
    count_prescribed = count_prescribed[1],
    count_realised = mean(count_realised),
    shortfall_pct = round(mean(shortfall_pct), 1)
  ),
  by = id_trans
][trans_names, on = "id_trans", nomatch = NULL][order(-shortfall_pct)][
  , .(name_anterior, name_posterior, count_prescribed, count_realised, shortfall_pct)
]
```

## (c1) Fuzzy similarity of differences

`calc_transition_similarity()` is evoland's port of Dinamica's "similarity of differences"
(Hagen 2003): for one transition it builds the observed and simulated **change** maps, and gives
each changed cell a membership in the other map's change that decays with the distance to the
nearest change there (`exp(-d / 2)` within the window, 1 in the same cell), so a patch placed one
cell off still scores. Each direction is averaged over that map's own changed cells only;
`similarity` is the minimum of the two directions, so a simulation cannot score well by placing
much more or much less change than was observed.

The focal operations dominate this step, so it runs on the daemons too, one member per task.

```{r}
#| label: backcast-fuzzy
fuzzy_one_run <- function(id_run_member, db_path, viable_trans, id_period_initial,
                          id_period_final, fuzzy_window) {
  db <- evoland::evoland_db$new(path = db_path, id_run = 0L, read_only = TRUE)
  rast_initial <- db$lulc_data_as_rast(id_period = id_period_initial)
  rast_observed <- db$lulc_data_as_rast(id_period = id_period_final)
  db$id_run <- id_run_member
  rast_simulated <- db$lulc_data_as_rast(id_period = id_period_final)

  res <- mapply(
    FUN = evoland::calc_transition_similarity,
    from_class = viable_trans$id_lulc_anterior,
    to_class = viable_trans$id_lulc_posterior,
    MoreArgs = list(
      initial_map = rast_initial,
      observed_map = rast_observed,
      simulated_map = rast_simulated,
      window_size = fuzzy_window,
      use_exp_decay = TRUE,
      decay_divisor = 2.0
    ),
    SIMPLIFY = FALSE
  )
  data.table::data.table(
    id_run = id_run_member,
    id_trans = viable_trans$id_trans,
    similarity = vapply(res, \(x) as.numeric(x$similarity), numeric(1L)),
    n_observed = vapply(res, \(x) as.numeric(x$n_observed), numeric(1L)),
    n_simulated = vapply(res, \(x) as.numeric(x$n_simulated), numeric(1L))
  )
}

fuzzy_dt <- mirai::mirai_map(
  member_runs$id_run,
  fuzzy_one_run,
  .args = list(
    db_path = db_path,
    viable_trans = viable_trans[, .(id_trans, id_lulc_anterior, id_lulc_posterior)],
    id_period_initial = id_period_initial,
    id_period_final = id_period_final,
    fuzzy_window = fuzzy_window
  )
)[.stop] |>
  rbindlist()
mirai::daemons(0)

run_param_set <- member_runs[, .(id_run, param_set)]
fuzzy_by_param <- run_param_set[fuzzy_dt, on = "id_run"][, .(
  similarity_sd = sd(similarity, na.rm = TRUE),
  similarity = mean(similarity, na.rm = TRUE),
  n_observed = mean(n_observed),
  n_simulated = mean(n_simulated)
), by = .(param_set, id_trans)]

fuzzy_by_param[trans_names, on = "id_trans", nomatch = NULL][order(param_set, similarity)][, .(
  param_set, name_anterior, name_posterior,
  similarity = round(similarity, 3),
  n_observed, n_simulated = round(n_simulated)
)]
```

## (c2) Cross-tabulation and figure of merit

The cross-tabulation of observed against simulated end class, restricted to the cells that
*should* have changed, decomposes into the four quantities of Pontius' figure of merit:

| | simulated persistence | simulated a change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **observed a change to _v_** | miss (A) | **hit (B)** if simulated to _v_, wrong class (C) otherwise |
| **observed persistence** | correct null | false alarm (D) |

$\mathrm{FoM} = B / (A + B + C + D)$ — the intersection of observed and simulated change over
their union. It ignores the correct-null cell, which is why it is the right statistic here.

**Glacier cells are excluded.** Their change is imposed from the record (see (b)), so a cell that
starts or ends as glacier is a hit by construction and says nothing about the model.

```{r}
#| label: backcast-fom
fom_args <- list(
  id_period_anterior = id_period_initial,
  id_period_post = id_period_final,
  id_run_reference = 0L,
  id_run_simulated = member_runs$id_run,
  exclude_id_lulc = id_lulc_glacier
)
fom_by_run <- do.call(db$figure_of_merit_v, fom_args)
fom_by_trans_run <- do.call(db$figure_of_merit_v, c(fom_args, by_transition = TRUE))

fom_by_run[order(-figure_of_merit), .(
  id_run, hits, wrong_hits, misses, false_alarms,
  figure_of_merit = round(figure_of_merit, 4),
  figure_of_merit_null = round(figure_of_merit_null, 4),
  producers_accuracy = round(producers_accuracy, 3),
  users_accuracy = round(users_accuracy, 3)
)]
```

The observed-against-simulated cross-tabulation of the backcast period, pooled over the members of
the best-estimate set, shows where the misses go:

```{r}
#| label: backcast-crosstab
crosstab_obs_sim <- rbindlist(lapply(member_runs[param_set == 1L, id_run], function(r) {
  db$lulc_crosstab_v(
    id_period_anterior = id_period_final,
    id_period_post = id_period_final,
    id_run_anterior = 0L,
    id_run_post = r
  )
}))[, .(n_cells = sum(n_cells) / sum(member_runs$param_set == 1L)), by = .(id_lulc_anterior, id_lulc_posterior)][
  lulc_names, on = c(id_lulc_anterior = "id_lulc"), observed := i.name
][
  lulc_names, on = c(id_lulc_posterior = "id_lulc"), simulated := i.name
]
dcast(crosstab_obs_sim, observed ~ simulated, value.var = "n_cells", fill = 0, fun.aggregate = sum)
```

The null — the FoM of a model that gets the quantity right but the location purely by chance —
is available in closed form. Within an anterior class $u$ of $N_u$ cells, of which the model
converts $S_{uv}$ to $v$ and the record converts $O_{uv}$, random placement gives
$\mathbb{E}[B_{uv}] = S_{uv} O_{uv} / N_u$, and the expected union of change over the class is
$S_u + O_u - S_u O_u / N_u$; `figure_of_merit_v()` returns it as `figure_of_merit_null`.

```{r}
#| label: backcast-fom-by-trans
fom_by_trans <- run_param_set[fom_by_trans_run, on = "id_run"][
  ,
  .(
    observed = mean(observed),
    simulated = mean(simulated),
    hits = mean(hits),
    figure_of_merit_null = mean(figure_of_merit_null)
  ),
  by = .(param_set, id_lulc_anterior, id_lulc_posterior)
][, figure_of_merit := hits / (observed + simulated - hits)][
  , at_chance := is.finite(figure_of_merit) & is.finite(figure_of_merit_null) &
    figure_of_merit <= figure_of_merit_null
]

fom_by_trans[
  trans_names, on = c("id_lulc_anterior", "id_lulc_posterior"), nomatch = NULL
][order(param_set, figure_of_merit)][, .(
  param_set, name_anterior, name_posterior,
  observed = round(observed), simulated = round(simulated),
  figure_of_merit = round(figure_of_merit, 3),
  figure_of_merit_null = round(figure_of_merit_null, 3),
  at_chance
)]
```

## (c3) Expected figure of merit over the replicate ensemble

Averaging the counts over the replicates of a parameter set gives the expected hits, misses, wrong
hits and false alarms, and the FoM computed from those is the ensemble expectation rather than
one sample of it (the mean of the per-run ratios would not be).

```{r}
#| label: backcast-ensemble-fom
ensemble_fom <- run_param_set[fom_by_run, on = "id_run"][, .(
  n_runs = .N,
  hits = mean(hits),
  wrong_hits = mean(wrong_hits),
  misses = mean(misses),
  false_alarms = mean(false_alarms),
  fom_null = mean(figure_of_merit_null)
), by = param_set][, fom_expected := hits / (hits + wrong_hits + misses + false_alarms)]

ensemble_fom[order(-fom_expected)]
```

## Acceptance criteria

Three, in the order they should be read. The first is a hard gate on the machinery; the second
is the substantive one; the third governs how the results may be reported.

1. **Quantity fidelity.** For every viable transition with `count_prescribed > 1000`, the
   replicate-mean shortfall must be below 5 %. A larger shortfall means the allocator could not
   deliver a demand taken straight from the observed record, and nothing downstream —
   least of all `090`, where the LP pushes rates *above* that record — can be trusted until it is
   understood.
2. **Allocation skill.** The ensemble FoM must beat the random-within-class null by a factor of
   two. Published land-change models mostly land between a few per cent and ~15 % absolute FoM
   (Pontius et al. 2008, *Ann. Reg. Sci.* 42), and absolute FoM scales with how much change
   there is to get right, so the only meaningful comparison is against a null on this same
   landscape and period.
3. **Per-transition honesty.** Transitions flagged `at_chance` above must be reported as
   spatially uninformative. Their quantity is still prescribed and still lands, but their
   *pattern* is noise, and `090d` must not present maps of them as model output.

```{r}
#| label: backcast-acceptance
quantity_gate <- quantity[
  count_prescribed > 1000,
  .(mean_shortfall_pct = mean(shortfall_pct)),
  by = id_trans
][mean_shortfall_pct > 5]

skill_gate <- ensemble_fom[, .(param_set, fom_expected, fom_null, ratio = fom_expected / fom_null)]

if (nrow(quantity_gate) > 0L) {
  warning("Quantity gate failed for ", nrow(quantity_gate), " transitions - see quantity_gate")
}
if (all(skill_gate$ratio < 2)) {
  warning(
    "No parameter set reaches 2x the random-allocation null (best ratio ",
    signif(max(skill_gate$ratio), 3),
    "). The predictor set, not the allocation parameters, is the thing to revisit."
  )
}
list(quantity_gate = quantity_gate, skill_gate = skill_gate)
```

## Select the parameter set and promote it

The winner is chosen on the ensemble FoM, with the mean `similarity` as the tie-break: FoM answers
"are the right cells changing", the fuzzy similarity answers "is the change the right shape", and
only the first is comparable against a null.

What is promoted to run `0` — where every SSP run inherits it — is **re-estimated from every
observed transition**, now including the last one; the winning set contributes only its
perturbation, i.e. its per-transition `frac_expander` offset from the hold-out best estimate.

```{r}
#| label: backcast-select
param_score <- merge(
  ensemble_fom[, .(param_set, fom_expected, fom_null)],
  fuzzy_by_param[, .(similarity = mean(similarity, na.rm = TRUE)), by = param_set],
  by = "param_set"
)[order(-fom_expected, -similarity)]

best_param <- param_score$param_set[1]
message("Selected parameter set ", best_param)
param_score
```

```{r}
#| label: backcast-commit-params
# Record each set's measured similarity alongside its parameters
db$alloc_params_t <- as_alloc_params_t(merge(
  copy(alloc_params)[, id_run := param_run_id(param_set)][, -"similarity"],
  fuzzy_by_param[, .(param_set, id_trans, similarity)],
  by = c("param_set", "id_trans"),
  all.x = TRUE
)[, -"param_set"])

expander_offset <- merge(
  alloc_params[param_set == best_param, .(id_trans, frac_expander)],
  best_estimate[, .(id_trans, frac_expander_best = frac_expander)],
  by = "id_trans"
)[, .(id_trans, offset = frac_expander - frac_expander_best)]

db$id_run <- 0L
promoted <- db$create_alloc_params_t()[expander_offset, on = "id_trans", offset := i.offset][
  is.na(offset), offset := 0
][, frac_expander := pmin(1, pmax(0, frac_expander + offset))][
  , frac_patcher := 1 - frac_expander
][, -"offset"]
db$alloc_params_t <- as_alloc_params_t(merge(
  promoted[, -"similarity"],
  fuzzy_by_param[param_set == best_param, .(id_trans, similarity)],
  by = "id_trans",
  all.x = TRUE
))
db$alloc_params_t
```

> **Why not `eval_alloc_params_t()`?** The upstream helper does this loop — allocate the
> observed periods per parameter set, then score with `calc_transition_similarity()` — but it
> calls `alloc_dinamica()`, does not use the `runs_t` hierarchy, runs one realisation per set and
> reports no figure of merit. See `TODO.md`, upstream asks.

```{r}
#| label: backcast-report
db$reporting_t <- as_reporting_t(data.table::rowwiseDT(
  key = , value = ,
  "backcast_period", as.character(id_period_final),
  "backcast_initial_period", as.character(id_period_initial),
  "backcast_calibration_periods", paste(calibration_periods, collapse = ","),
  "backcast_n_param_sets", as.character(length(param_sets)),
  "backcast_n_replicates", as.character(n_replicates),
  "backcast_perturb_sd", as.character(perturb_sd),
  "backcast_fuzzy_window", as.character(fuzzy_window),
  "backcast_selected_param_set", as.character(best_param),
  "backcast_fom_expected", as.character(signif(param_score$fom_expected[1], 4)),
  "backcast_fom_null", as.character(signif(param_score$fom_null[1], 4)),
  "backcast_similarity", as.character(signif(param_score$similarity[1], 4)),
  "backcast_unmodellable_pct", as.character(signif(max(unmodellable$unmodellable_pct), 3))
))
```
